Subject: High 5xxs & TTL spikes to Redwood API - impacting checkout

Vanessa,

We're seeing a sharp increase in 5xx errors and multi-second response times for calls to your /v1/generate endpoint from our US-East nodes starting ~08:45 PT. Checkout conversions are dropping and retries are starting to pile up. Sample request IDs and timestamps attached.

What we have observed:
- 60% increase in p50 latency (from 180ms -> 1.2s)
- ~7% of calls returning 502/504 over the last 25 minutes
- Errors appear to correlate with requests routed through our VPC peering path to your dedicated endpoints

Can you confirm whether there are known issues on your side or if this might be related to our peering/NAT? We need an ETA on restoration; this is affecting our peak checkout window.

Attaching: brightline-request-samples.json

— Alex Monroe, SRE (Brightline Retail)

On Sat, May 22, 2027 at 09:19 AM vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai wrote:
> I'll keep this thread as the single point of truth and post updates every 20 minutes.

Quick summary of what I see from the dedicated pool that serves Brightline:
- Firewall/proxy (egress) logs show repeated 502/504 responses between 08:42-09:10 PT from our edge proxy cluster in us-east-1. See attached redwood-firewall-logs-20270522.csv.
- Packet capture from one affected worker shows elevated TCP retransmits and RSTs; sample attached (pcap).
- DNS lookups to Brightline's resolver (10.2.3.4 per their traceroutes) are experiencing 200-800ms tails — not our authoritative DNS but seems to affect connection setup time.
- No recent code rollout or model change detected in the 45m window. Autoscaling added 3 workers at 08:50 but those additions overlapped with the beginning of the spike.

Hypothesis: combination of intermittent peering route flaps at the Brightline->cloud provider fabric plus their upstream DNS resolver intermittently timing out, which exacerbates connection count and triggers proxy timeouts in our edge tier.

Immediate mitigations applied (09:34 PT):
- Bypassed one problematic proxy node via routing policy for Brightline traffic (temporary).
- Enabled aggressive keepalive on maintained connections to reduce new TCP handshakes.

Next actions:
- Request Brightline to validate peering route health and their NAT gateway metrics.
- We'll keep proxy bypass active and collect 30m of telemetry.

— Dylan
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: High 5xxs & TTL spikes to Redwood API - customer update

Alex — sharing what we know and the immediate plan in one paragraph for your CTO:

At 08:42 PT we observed a sharp increase in TCP retransmits and proxy 502/504s for traffic between Brightline's US-East peered network and our us-east dedicated pool. Our infra team temporarily bypassed one edge proxy node and enabled connection keepalives; those mitigations reduced 5xxs by ~80% within 20 minutes. Current hypothesis (moderate confidence): intermittent peering route instability combined with elevated DNS tails on Brightline's upstream resolver led to connection churn that overwhelmed one proxy instance. Next steps we recommend together: Brightline validate VPC peering routes/NAT throttling and consider rotating to the secondary resolver; we will keep the proxy bypass for 2 hours and open a cloud provider fabric ticket if instability persists.

Action items and owners:
- Brightline (Alex): run traceroutes/mtr from affected nodes to our peering IPs and share results; validate resolver latency and NAT gateway metrics.
- Dylan (Redwood): maintain proxy bypass and collect 2 hours of telemetry; if errors rebound, escalate to cloud provider (PD-98321).
- Marissa (Redwood): monitor dedicated pool capacity and scale if queue depth rises beyond thresholds.

Attachments: sample packet capture and firewall logs for your SREs. We'll keep you posted every 30 minutes until fully stable. Apologies for the disruption — we know this is impacting checkout.

— Vanessa Ortiz
